items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had been part of the Ron Carter quartet... It was Ben who came up with the idea of Charlie Rouse... We got a gig and called Rouse. He made the gig, and it was a perfect fit... We existed for a long time, until Rouse passed away... We had a good run with that particular band.

ctx.x: . . . and Ben had already had the trio. For me, this was important. This was one of – this album and – this was key in my development. So if you could let the public know about the development of Sphere and give us that story.

It started out – as you mentioned, we had the trio, Ben Riley, Buster Williams, and myself. We had been part of the Ron Carter quartet, that rhythm section. When Ron broke the band up, we continued to work as a trio and also as a rhythm section for other guys who were coming to town, Eddie Harris or Lockjaw [Eddie Davis] and Sweets [Harry Edison]. We would be their rhythm section. So we said, maybe we should just get a horn player and have a quartet. It was Ben who came up with the idea of Charlie Rouse. He said,…
